FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Non-Powered Material Handling Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IATA/AHM 924 'Functional specifications for heavy item lift platform' issued by International Air Transport Association (IATA). For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 APRIL 2005 TO IS 13951 : 1994 HEAVY ITEM LIFT PLATFORM FOR AIRCRAFT/AIRPORT OPERATIONS -- GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
( Page 1, clause 3.9 ) -- Substitute the following for the existing: 'The lifting mechanism shall be capable of raising the platform of the unit plus specified load up to any point within the range specified in 3.1 by any suitable means (powered or non-powered).' ( ME 07 )
Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India

IS 13951 : 1994

Indian Standard HEAVY ITEM LIFT PLATFORM FOR AIRCRAFT/AIRPORT OPERATIONS -- GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the general requirements for a towable lift platform used for lifting and lowering heavy items into/from lower deck compartments of conventional aircraft not equipped with integrated powered loading systems. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standard IS 12863 : 1989 'Symbols for the pictorial standardization of aircraft cargo handling system for unit load devices' is a necessary adjunct to this standard. 3 CONSTRUCTION AND OVERALL DIMENSIONS 3.1 On an adequate chassis the lift shall provide a platform having height range between 500 mm and 3 000 mm for loading operations from ground level to maximum feature heights including second stack loading on freight transporter and containers on board including gallery. 3.2 The overall dimensions of the unit shall be kept to a minimum considering the minimum platform dimensions of 700 � 1 200 mm. Considerations shall be given to Option 8.4, if applicable. 3.3 The lifting capacity is 10 kN (1 000 kg) minimum. The platform shall be designed for a minimum load concentration of 7.35 kN/m2 (750 kgf/m2). 3.4 The unit shall have adequate under-clearance from any portion of the equipment to the ground when negotiating two ramps that intersect at 5� and provide total stability with the platform at any raised height and the loads of any type on platform. 3.5 The wheels are steerable with the towbar providing the maximum possible manoeuvrability for the unit. 3.6 The towbar eye fits the coupling most commonly used on airport equipment. 3.7 The chassis is equipped with a coupling or tow hitch which allows the link with other movable airport equipment. 3.8 In its upright position the towbar engages the parking brake. In this position it is secured against inadvertent falling down. 3.9 The lifting mechanism shall be capable of raising the platform of the unit plus specified load up to any point within the range specified in 3.1 by means of a powered hydraulic system. 4 PLATFORM DESIGN 4.1 The platform shall be 1 200 mm long and 700 mm wide (overall dimensions). Consideration shall be given to Option 8.4, if a applicable. 4.2 The platform deck shall be completely covered with anti-skid material. 5 PLATFORM OPERATION 5.1 The platform shall be designed for being towered into the desired position by a tow tug commonly used on airports. The unit shall be operated by one person (operator). 5.2 The time taken for the platform to reach maximum height, from the lowered position and vice versa, that is, one complete cycles, shall not exceed two minutes. 5.3 The platform controls shall be accessible from the ground at all times. 6 MOBILITY AND STABILITY 6.1 The unit shall be mobile and stable with or without load on platform at lower height up to towing speed of 15 km/h. 6.2 The platform shall be capable of turning 180� within 1 200 mm radius. 7 CONTROLS 7.1 All controls necessary to operate the platform conveyor system shall be located in the operator's stand (see IS 12863 : 1989). 7.2 Provisions should be made to operate the platform controls from ground also, at all times.

1

IS 13951 : 1994 8 OPTIONS 8.1 Platform surface equipped with rollers. 8.2 Platform surface equipped with balls. 8.3 Platform surface equipped with a conveyor belt. 8.4 Platform extension up to 200 mm lengthwise and/or up to 1 500 mm widthwise. 8.5 In order to provide for additional stability at least chocks should be provided and attached to the unit in such a way that they cannot be lost. 8.6 Stabilizers to provide for stability during loading/unloading operations. 8.7 Guard rails (in case of patform extensions). 9 SAFETY REQUIREMENTS 9.1 While in operation, the lift platform shall be provided with a foil safe locking arrangement to prevent the platform from slipping down from any position by means of hydraulically operated ratchet locking mechanism provided with the hydraulic lifting cylinder. 9.2 Provision shall be made to stop the downward movement of ram piston in the case of failure of hydraulic hoses. Pilot operated check valves mounted on hydraulic cylinders are recommended. 9.3 Provision shall also be made to stop the movement of the platform within 5 mm from the aircraft body. Proximity switches are recommended for this purposes.

Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such a review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Addition'.
